text: The paper reports that instructing debaters to disagree ('tit for tat', higher disagreement) is necessary for good MAD performance, but the instruction 'must disagree with each other on every point' (disagreement 0.988) does not give the best performance. The authors speculate that constant disagreement causes polarization, where debate becomes about winning rather than seeking truth.
title: Moderate disagreement helps MAD; forced disagreement on every point does not
